title: Checks for inplace=True usages in pandas function and method calls.
summary: Using inplace=True encourages mutation rather than immutable data, which is harder to reason about and may cause bugs. It also removes the ability to use the method chaining style for pandas operations. Ruff takes this rule from pandas-vet and made it stable in v0.0.188.
message_templates: `inplace=True` should be avoided; it has inconsistent behavior

title: Checks for uses of .isnull on Pandas objects.
summary: In the Pandas API, .isna and .isnull are equivalent. For consistency, prefer .isna over .isnull. Ruff takes this rule from pandas-vet and made it stable in v0.0.188.
message_templates: `.isna` is preferred to `.isnull`; functionality is equivalent

title: Checks for uses of .notnull on Pandas objects.
summary: In the Pandas API, .notna and .notnull are equivalent. For consistency, prefer .notna over .notnull. Ruff takes this rule from pandas-vet and made it stable in v0.0.188.
message_templates: `.notna` is preferred to `.notnull`; functionality is equivalent

title: Checks for uses of .ix on Pandas objects.
summary: The .ix method is deprecated as its behavior is ambiguous. Specifically, it's often unclear whether .ix is indexing by label or by ordinal position. Ruff takes this rule from pandas-vet and made it stable in v0.0.188.
message_templates: `.ix` is deprecated; use more explicit `.loc` or `.iloc`

title: Checks for uses of .at on Pandas objects.
summary: The .at method selects a single value from a DataFrame or Series based on a label index, and is slightly faster than using .loc. However, .loc is more idiomatic and versatile, as it can be used to select multiple values at once. Ruff takes this rule from pandas-vet and made it stable in v0.0.188.
message_templates: Use `.loc` instead of `.at`. If speed is important, use NumPy.

title: Checks for uses of .iat on Pandas objects.
summary: The .iat method selects a single value from a DataFrame or Series based on an ordinal index, and is slightly faster than using .iloc. However, .iloc is more idiomatic and versatile, as it can be used to select multiple values at once. Ruff takes this rule from pandas-vet and made it stable in v0.0.188.
message_templates: Use `.iloc` instead of `.iat`. If speed is important, use NumPy.

title: Checks for uses of .pivot or .unstack on Pandas objects.
summary: Prefer .pivot_table to .pivot or .unstack. .pivot_table is more general and can be used to implement the same behavior as .pivot and .unstack. Ruff takes this rule from pandas-vet and made it stable in v0.0.188.
message_templates: `.pivot_table` is preferred to `.pivot` or `.unstack`; provides same functionality

title: Checks for uses of .values on Pandas Series and Index objects.
summary: The .values attribute is ambiguous as its return type is unclear. As such, it is no longer recommended by the Pandas documentation. Ruff takes this rule from pandas-vet and made it stable in v0.0.188.

title: Checks for uses of pd.read_table to read CSV files.
summary: In the Pandas API, pd.read_csv and pd.read_table are equivalent apart from their default separator: pd.read_csv defaults to a comma (,), while pd.read_table defaults to a tab (\t) as the default separator. Ruff takes this rule from pandas-vet and made it stable in v0.0.188.
message_templates: Use `.read_csv` instead of `.read_table` to read CSV files

title: Checks for uses of .stack on Pandas objects.
summary: Prefer .melt to .stack, which has the same functionality but with support for direct column renaming and no dependence on MultiIndex. Ruff takes this rule from pandas-vet and made it stable in v0.0.188.
message_templates: `.melt` is preferred to `.stack`; provides same functionality

title: Checks for uses of pd.merge on Pandas objects.
summary: In Pandas, the .merge method (exposed on, e.g., DataFrame objects) and the pd.merge function (exposed on the Pandas module) are equivalent. Ruff takes this rule from pandas-vet and made it stable in v0.0.188.
message_templates: Use `.merge` method instead of `pd.merge` function. They have equivalent functionality.

title: Check for uses of .nunique() to check if a Pandas Series is constant (i.e., contains only one unique value).
summary: .nunique() is computationally inefficient for checking if a Series is constant. Ruff takes this rule from pandas-vet and made it stable in v0.0.279.
message_templates: Using `series.nunique()` for checking that a series is constant is inefficient

title: Checks for assignments to the variable df.
summary: Although df is a common variable name for a Pandas DataFrame, it's not a great variable name for production code, as it's non-descriptive and prone to name conflicts. Ruff takes this rule from pandas-vet, and removed it.
message_templates: Avoid using the generic variable name `df` for DataFrames
